scenarios.journey: platform foundations — access gate application refused
scenarios.test: 2. Application form validates at least one link required
scenarios.expects: A complete-looking application with no trading link is REFUSED with 'Please provide at least one link'; it never advances.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — access gate application received
scenarios.test: 3. Application submitted with website link
scenarios.expects: An application carrying a website link reaches the 'Application Received' confirmation.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — access gate operator review
scenarios.test: 4. Admin sees application
scenarios.expects: A submitted application is visible in the Super Admin Applications surface.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — access gate approval creates onboarding
scenarios.test: 6. Admin approves a partner application
scenarios.expects: Approving confirms the application and creates ONE onboarding record keyed to the SAME tenant id the brand login card uses (brand-app-app-0001), and the brand then enters its portal.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — access gate rejection

scenarios.expects: Rejecting confirms '<name> rejected' and the row's decision actions are gone, because the application is no longer pending.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — RBAC hides super-only destinations
scenarios.test: Non-super Admin does not see super-only views in the nav
scenarios.expects: The admin rail hides Super Admin, Audit Log and Integration Settings from a non-super admin while keeping Brand CRM and Billing.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — RBAC hides admin-only destinations from a brand
scenarios.test: Brand — admin-only views hidden; render-side auth intact
scenarios.expects: The brand rail hides Audit Log, Super Admin and Integration Settings.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — a cold deep link keeps its address
scenarios.test: a cold product deep link keeps its address and lands on the requested view
scenarios.expects: A cold product deep link keeps its address and shows the login entry; after the one-click demo login the REQUESTED view renders.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — session survives a refresh
scenarios.test: F5 in place stays in place (no silent sign-out)
scenarios.expects: After login a refresh keeps the same product view and the login entry does not return.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — Back/Forward stay in the product
scenarios.test: Back/Forward move between product views instead of leaving the app
scenarios.expects: Browser Back and Forward move between product views rather than leaving the application.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — a removed address fails closed
scenarios.test: the removed carrier address fails closed (no carrier shell exists)
scenarios.expects: The removed /carrier/manifest address resolves to the public site (fail-closed): the public entry renders, no product nav exists and no carrier surface is resurrected.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — RBAC refuses a Super-Admin-only view at render
scenarios.test: a tier that may not enter an environment is refused (AccessDenied, not the panel)
scenarios.expects: A Mercenta Admin may enter the admin environment but a Super-Admin-only view addressed by URL renders 'Super Admin Access Required', not the panel.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — a tampered session fails closed
scenarios.test: a tampered or unknown persisted session fails CLOSED
scenarios.expects: A brand-tier session claiming the admin environment, an unknown tenant and a malformed stored value are each refused on restore — never half-restored.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — a public address stays public with a live session
scenarios.test: is still the public marketing homepage
scenarios.expects: `/` remains the public marketing homepage both with and without a live session; the address decides the environment.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — tenant isolation on purchase orders
scenarios.test: Brand A cannot see Brand B POs
scenarios.expects: The brand's PO surface shows its OWN POs and none of another brand's (PO-9002 / PO-9003 absent).

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — tenant isolation on messages
scenarios.test: Brand A cannot see Brand B messages
scenarios.expects: The brand's support surface renders with no other brand's name or messages present.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — tenant isolation on the payout ledger
scenarios.test: payout ledger is tenant-scoped
scenarios.expects: A brand's payout ledger holds its OWN rows and none of another brand's.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — cross-tenant read is admin-only
scenarios.test: Admin can see all brands
scenarios.expects: Cross-tenant reads are admin-only: the admin surface lists more than one brand.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the carrier console is admin-only
scenarios.test: the carrier tenant is gone and the carrier console is admin-only
scenarios.expects: A brand session reaches its OWN Logistics Hub but never the Mercenta-side carrier console.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the Audit Log surface is accessible
scenarios.test: 4. Audit log is structurally sound and scan-clean
scenarios.expects: The Admin Audit Log surface passes the structural skeleton and the accessibility scan.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the Audit Log surface renders
scenarios.test: 5. Audit log renders
scenarios.expects: The Audit Log destination opens the 'Admin Audit Log' surface for a Super Admin.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — an on-behalf action is attributed
scenarios.test: 6. On-behalf actions are attributed in the audit log
scenarios.expects: A real on-behalf admin action (a fulfillment-track override) writes the 'fulfillment_track_override' entry visible in the Audit Log.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — a money-path action is audited
scenarios.test: settling a payout reports mock mode, clears it from pending and audits it
scenarios.expects: Settling a commission payout writes the canonical audit row ('commission_payout_settled'), visible in the Super Admin-only Audit Log.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the seven public pages render, take the shell and publish no internal detail
scenarios.test: shell and publishes no internal detail
scenarios.expects: Each of the seven public pages renders its H1, takes the expected shell theme under both themes, has no horizontal overflow at 390 and publishes no red-line claim.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the public footer carries the canonical categories
scenarios.test: the footer carries the five-column shape
scenarios.expects: The footer carries the owner's five columns and EXACTLY the canonical APPROVED_CATEGORIES list (read from the owner, not retyped).

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the cookie notice choice sticks
scenarios.test: answering the notice STICKS across a reload
scenarios.expects: Answering the cookie notice sticks across a reload and the footer can re-open it.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — public chrome labels agree with their owner
scenarios.test: the footer agrees with them
scenarios.expects: The header publishes the owner's nav labels and every footer link uses the SAME label for the same route.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the design system kit renders
scenarios.test: canonical kit renders
scenarios.expects: Super Admin → Design System renders the canonical kit (typography, buttons, statuses, alerts, forms, tabs, table).

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — keyboard focus-visible is present
scenarios.test: focus-visible outline is visible on keyboard focus of a Button
scenarios.expects: A canonical Button shows a visible keyboard focus-visible outline.

scenarios.journey: platform foundations — the design system has no horizontal overflow
scenarios.test: (no horizontal overflow)
scenarios.expects: The Design System surface has no horizontal overflow at each target viewport.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — acquisition pipeline — brand to CRM
scenarios.test: 1. Real BI brand → ICP → approval → simulated send → response → opportunity → CRM
scenarios.expects: A real Brand-Intelligence brand runs the whole acquisition journey — ICP qualification, approval, a SIMULATED outreach send, a response, an opportunity and a CRM relationship — end to end.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — acquisition — relationship recorded where it is read
scenarios.test: 1b. The relationship is visible in the CRM and in the ONE canonical Messages thread
scenarios.expects: The acquisition relationship is visible both in the CRM record and in the ONE canonical Messages thread — the surface reads the canonical record, not a copy.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — acquisition — rejection is a real distinct outcome
scenarios.test: 2. REJECT is a real, distinct approval outcome on a second real brand
scenarios.expects: REJECT is a real, distinct approval outcome on a second real brand — it is recorded and never silently treated as approved.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — acquisition — a brand tenant cannot see acquisition
scenarios.test: 3. Tenant isolation — a brand session has no acquisition surface and no prospect thread
scenarios.expects: A brand tenant session has NO acquisition surface and no prospect thread — cross-tenant acquisition data is refused by construction.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial model — onboarding offers both and honours the choice
scenarios.test: 1. onboarding offers both models and honours the recorded selection
scenarios.expects: Onboarding offers BOTH commercial models and honours the recorded selection — an undeclared model is never defaulted.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial model — a change needs an actor and a reason
scenarios.test: 2. Super Admin records a model change with a reason, and it is audited
scenarios.expects: Only a Super Admin may change the commercial relationship, every change carries a reason, and the change produces an audit record.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial model — the brand sees only its own terms
scenarios.test: 3. the brand sees its own relationship read-only
scenarios.expects: The brand sees its OWN commercial relationship read-only, with the separation from the channel compliance documents stated; it never sees another brand terms.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial readiness — every canonical product with owner and next step
scenarios.test: 1. the Control Centre Commercial section shows every canonical product
scenarios.expects: The Founder Control Centre Commercial section shows every canonical product with its route, owner, deadline and next step.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial readiness — opening a product explains WHY
scenarios.test: 2. opening a product explains WHY — the evaluated conditions, the missing information and the canonical work item
scenarios.expects: Opening a product explains WHY: the evaluated conditions, the missing information and the canonical work item behind the status.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial readiness — a brand never reaches the Control Centre
scenarios.test: 3. RBAC — a brand session never reaches the Founder Control Centre or its commercial data
scenarios.expects: A brand session NEVER reaches the Founder Control Centre or its commercial data — the role restriction fails closed.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial readiness — a brand sees only its own products
scenarios.test: 4. the brand sees ONLY its own products, explained in plain language with a guide
scenarios.expects: A brand sees ONLY its own products, explained in plain language with a guide — no other tenant products appear.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial readiness — a repeat action is idempotent
scenarios.test: 5. a REAL brand action changes the product status, a repeat does not, and the journey reaches ready
scenarios.expects: A REAL brand action advances the product status; repeating it does NOT double-advance, and the journey reaches ready — the transition is idempotent.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — commercial readiness — a clear product states its next stage
scenarios.test: 6. a product with no outstanding action says so, and its next step is the declared next stage
scenarios.expects: A product with no outstanding action says so and names the declared next stage — an empty state is honest, never blank.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — conversion gate — a bot submission is refused and nothing recorded
scenarios.test: 1. a filled honeypot is refused and NOTHING is recorded
scenarios.expects: A submission that fills the honeypot control is REFUSED and NOTHING is recorded — a bot can never create an application.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — conversion gate — a too-fast submission is refused
scenarios.test: 2. a submission faster than the declared minimum is refused
scenarios.expects: A submission completed faster than the declared minimum time is refused — the timing rule is enforced at the boundary.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — conversion gate — invalid answers refused per field
scenarios.test: 3. invalid answers produce per-field, announced refusals
scenarios.expects: Invalid answers produce per-field, announced refusals — each field names its own error and the refusal is read aloud.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — conversion gate — the compulsory phone is required
scenarios.test: 3b. a MISSING phone number is refused under the phone control (it is compulsory)
scenarios.expects: A MISSING phone number is refused under the phone control — the compulsory field cannot be skipped.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — conversion gate — a duplicate application is recorded once
scenarios.test: 4. the same application is recorded ONCE, and the second attempt is told so
scenarios.expects: The same application is recorded ONCE; a second identical attempt does not create a duplicate and is told so.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — conversion gate — submission never waits for a hanging third party
scenarios.test: 5. submission never waits for the third-party link check (the hosts hang)
scenarios.expects: Submission NEVER waits for the third-party link check — a hanging provider cannot block the applicant (degraded provider fails soft).

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding hand-off — qualified opportunity to operational brand
scenarios.test: 1. Qualified opportunity → tenant identity → ordered steps → operational brand
scenarios.expects: A qualified opportunity becomes a tenant identity, ordered onboarding steps and an operational brand — the hand-off is one continuous, canonical path.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding hand-off — recorded in the Brand CRM relationship
scenarios.test: 2. The hand-off is visible in the Brand CRM relationship record
scenarios.expects: The hand-off is visible in the Brand CRM relationship record — the same identity, not a second competing record.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding hand-off — a brand tenant has no acquisition surface
scenarios.test: 3. A brand tenant session has no acquisition/onboarding surface
scenarios.expects: A brand tenant session has NO acquisition/onboarding surface — the operator-only path is refused to a tenant.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding workflow — admin drives onboarding to OPERATIONAL
scenarios.test: 1. Admin operates an acquisition-origin onboarding to OPERATIONAL in the pipeline
scenarios.expects: An admin operates an acquisition-origin onboarding to OPERATIONAL in the pipeline — acceptance, ordered steps and the operational end state.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding workflow — the pipeline is derived, never seeded
scenarios.test: 2. The pipeline is derived (0 when empty) and brand sessions cannot reach it
scenarios.expects: The onboarding pipeline is DERIVED (it reports 0 when empty, never a seeded number) and a brand session cannot reach it.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding workflow — manual creation to canonical record
scenarios.test: 3. Manual creation → canonical record → the brand tenant can enter its portal
scenarios.expects: A manual creation produces the canonical onboarding record and the brand tenant can then actually enter its portal.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding wizard — step 1 on a fresh brand
scenarios.test: 1. Fresh brand starts onboarding with step 1 visible
scenarios.expects: A fresh brand starts the onboarding wizard with step 1 (Brand Profile) visible and Continue available.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding wizard — the default recommendation steers to Financed
scenarios.test: 2. Track recommendation (default) steers to Financed
scenarios.expects: The default answers produce a System recommendation of the Financed track — the steer is shown, not hidden.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding wizard — working capital steers to Brand-direct
scenarios.test: steers to Brand-direct supply
scenarios.expects: Declaring working capital present steers the recommendation to Brand-direct supply — a different input yields the other declared track.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding wizard — both tracks are always offered
scenarios.test: 4. Step-4 cards expose both track options
scenarios.expects: Step 4 exposes BOTH fulfilment-track cards — the recommendation is advice, and the brand can choose either.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding wizard — the mandatory legal agreements are exposed
scenarios.test: 5. Walking to step 5 exposes the mandatory legal agreements
scenarios.expects: Step 5 exposes the mandatory legal agreements (logistics and chargeback) — the compliance documents are a gate on the wizard.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — onboarding wizard — admin override with a logged reason

scenarios.expects: An admin can OVERRIDE the fulfilment track, and the override requires a logged reason — an operator intervention is attributed.

scenarios.journey: onboarding & acquisition — opportunity discovery — vertical rollup and ranked list
